description: Changes #2, #6, #12 (backend): Make OpenRouter success/fallback transparent and expose true source/model. Change the LlmAdapter to return a richer per-call result {text, source, model, fallbackReason?} instead of a bare string, keep the deterministic fallback, log only non-secret diagnostics on failure (HTTP status + safe message; never headers, body, API key, or PII), extend /api/health and /api/customers/:id/explain to report the ACTUAL source and model used, and update the audit entry to record the true source. Update web/src/api/types.ts and client to match. Add tests (mocked fetch, no network).
steps: In server/src/adapters/openrouter.ts: define a result type, e.g. `export interface LlmResult { text: string; source: "openrouter" | "deterministic"; model: string; fallbackReason?: string; }`. Change the LlmAdapter interface methods explainDecision/draftRecoveryMessage to return Promise<LlmResult>.

DeterministicExplainer: keep the *Sync methods producing the text; wrap them so explainDecision/draftRecoveryMessage return { text, source: "deterministic", model: "deterministic" } (no fallbackReason since deterministic is the intended adapter when no key). Keep the sync methods exported/available for the OpenRouter fallback path.

OpenRouterAdapter: change private complete(prompt) to return a structured outcome capturing success (content + actual model from the API response's `model` field when present) or failure (with a non-secret reason: e.g. `HTTP 401` or `network error: <safe message>`). On non-2xx: read status (and optionally a short safe status text) but NEVER log or return headers, body, or the API key. On success but empty content: treat as fallback with reason 'empty completion'. explainDecision/draftRecoveryMessage then return either { text: llmText, source: "openrouter", model: actualOrConfiguredModel } on success, or { text: fallbackSyncText, source: "deterministic", model: config.model or "deterministic", fallbackReason } on failure.

When OPENROUTER_MODEL is a routing alias (e.g. 'openrouter/free') and the API returns an actual `model` in the response JSON, report that returned model rather than the configured alias where practical. Fall back to the configured model string if the response has none.

Add non-secret failure logging: on OpenRouter failure use console.warn with a message like `OpenRouter call failed (source=deterministic fallback): <reason>` including only HTTP status / safe message. Do NOT log the prompt content (may reference customer), the API key, headers, or the response body.

In server/src/api/app.ts /explain route: call llmAdapter.explainDecision and draftRecoveryMessage (now returning LlmResult). Derive the true source from the results (e.g. explanation.source). Respond with { source: <actual source used>, model: <actual model used>, outcome, explanation: explanation.text, recoveryMessage: recoveryMessage.text, fallbackReason?: explanation.fallbackReason }. The response `source` MUST reflect what actually produced the text, not llmAdapter.kind. A failed OpenRouter call must report source 'deterministic'.

Update the /explain audit entry detail/metadata to record the TRUE source and model actually used (e.g. detail `Generated explanation via <actualSource> (model <actualModel>).`, metadata { source: actualSource, model: actualModel, outcome, ...(fallbackReason ? { fallbackReason } : {}) }). Never put the API key in the audit log.

In server/src/api/app.ts /api/health route: extend the JSON to also expose the configured model and whether OpenRouter is enabled, e.g. { status, paymentMode, llm: llmAdapter.kind, model: <configured model or 'deterministic'>, aiMode: <'openrouter'|'deterministic'> }. To get the model into the app, thread it through AppDependencies (add optional `llmModel?: string` or pass the OpenRouterConfig-derived model) OR expose a `model` getter on the LlmAdapter interface (e.g. readonly model: string on both adapters). Prefer adding `readonly model: string` to LlmAdapter (deterministic -> 'deterministic', openrouter -> config.model) so health and dashboard can read it directly from the adapter. Update server.ts wiring if needed.
Update createLlmAdapter to set the model on each adapter accordingly.

Update web/src/api/types.ts: ExplainResponse gains `model: string` and optional `fallbackReason?: string`. Add a HealthResponse type (status, paymentMode, llm, model, aiMode). Ensure field names match backend exactly.
Update web/src/api/client.ts if a health call is needed by the UI (add api.getHealth() returning HealthResponse) — the dashboard mode indicators (FEAT-003) will consume it.

Update server/test/openrouter.test.ts and add coverage: (a) success path — construct OpenRouterAdapter with an apiKey config and a MOCK fetchImpl returning 200 with choices[0].message.content and a `model` field; assert result.source === 'openrouter', result.model === returned model, result.text === content. (b) failure path — mock fetch returning non-2xx (e.g. 401) OR throwing; assert result.source === 'deterministic', result.text equals the deterministic fallback text, and fallbackReason is set (mentions status/network). Do NOT hit the real network. (c) deterministic adapter returns source 'deterministic' and model 'deterministic'.

Update server/test/api.e2e.test.ts health test to assert the new fields (model + aiMode) alongside existing paymentMode/llm assertions; add an /explain shape assertion that the response includes source and model fields (deterministic in the e2e since it wires DeterministicExplainer).
Run `npm test` and `npm run build`; fix any type errors across server and web from the interface change.
acceptance_criteria: LlmAdapter methods return a structured result carrying the true source and model; deterministic fallback is preserved.
A failed OpenRouter call (non-2xx or thrown) results in deterministic text AND source reported as 'deterministic' with a fallbackReason; it is never reported as a successful LLM response.
On OpenRouter failure, only non-secret diagnostics are logged (HTTP status / safe message). No API key, headers, request/response body, or PII in logs.
GET /api/health returns the actual payment mode, ai mode/llm kind, and configured model.
POST /api/customers/:id/explain returns the actual source and model used (and fallbackReason when fallback occurred); the audit entry records the true source/model.
web/src/api/types.ts and client.ts match the new backend response shapes and build cleanly.
New/updated tests cover OpenRouter success, OpenRouter failure->fallback, and source/model reporting using a mocked fetch (no network). All tests pass.
verification: Run `npm test` from repo root; confirm all tests pass including new OpenRouter success/failure and health/explain shape tests.
Run `npm run build` and confirm zero errors in both server and web.
findings:
Implemented per plan. Added LlmResult { text, source, model, fallbackReason? } and readonly `model` on LlmAdapter. DeterministicExplainer.model = 'deterministic'; kept the *Sync helpers for the OpenRouter fallback path. OpenRouterAdapter.complete() now returns a structured CompletionOutcome: success carries content + the API-returned `model` (falls back to config.model when the response omits it, so routing aliases like 'openrouter/free' report the real resolved model); failures (no key / non-2xx / thrown / invalid JSON / empty completion) return a NON-SECRET reason ('HTTP <status>', 'network error: <safe msg>', 'invalid response JSON', 'empty completion'). Non-secret console.warn only; never logs prompt, key, headers, or bodies. app.ts /explain now derives source/model from the explanation LlmResult (honest: a failed OpenRouter call reports source 'deterministic' + fallbackReason), and the audit entry records the true source+model (never the key). /api/health now also returns `model` and `aiMode` alongside status/paymentMode/llm. web/src/api/types.ts: ExplainResponse gained model + optional fallbackReason; added HealthResponse. web/src/api/client.ts: added api.getHealth(). Tests: openrouter.test.ts updated to assert result.text/source/model and added mocked-fetch OpenRouter success (returned model, no-model->config.model, model getter) and failure (HTTP 401, thrown network error, empty completion, no-key-leak) coverage; api.e2e.test.ts health test asserts model+aiMode and a new /explain shape test asserts source+model (deterministic in e2e). Verification: `npm test` = 145 passed (was 137); `npm run build` zero errors in both server and web. The two stderr lines (payment.definitely_not_real, and the OpenRouter fallback warns) are expected negative-path/test output. Did NOT touch engine/financial/risk/decision logic or the 7 scenario outcomes. Did NOT commit/push (per instructions). FEAT-003 handles the React UI rendering of these fields.

FOLLOW-UP (review 2026-09-05-000600 Finding 2): the review noted the app.ts /explain wiring that surfaces fallbackReason + source:'deterministic' into the HTTP response body (and audit metadata) was only covered at the adapter unit level, with no end-to-end coverage of a live-OpenRouter-then-fallback path. FIX: added an e2e test to server/test/api.e2e.test.ts (supertest, like the existing suite) that builds a separate createApp(...) wired with a real OpenRouterAdapter whose fetchImpl is MOCKED to return HTTP 401 (no network). It seeds its own in-memory DB and asserts POST /api/customers/cust_transient/explain returns 200 with source==='deterministic', model==='openai/gpt-4o-mini' (configured model still named), non-empty explanation + recoveryMessage, outcome 'RECOVER', and a fallbackReason matching /HTTP 401|network error/. It also asserts the API key never appears in the response body, and that the persisted audit entry (action 'explanation_generated') records metadata.source==='deterministic', metadata.model==='openai/gpt-4o-mini', a matching fallbackReason, and no leaked key. The existing deterministic-intended /explain e2e assertion (no fallbackReason) is kept. Verified npm test = 150 passing (was 146), the OpenRouter fallback console.warn lines are expected negative-path output. Changed file this follow-up: server/test/api.e2e.test.ts.
